Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "118 :     public static FastDateFormat getInstance(String pattern) {\n119 :         return cache.getInstance(pattern, null, null);\n120 :     }"

The current bug report describes that `FastDateFormat`'s "z" pattern does not respect the timezone of `Calendar` instances passed to the `format()` method. Looking at the test case `testCalendarTimezoneRespected()`, it sets up two time zones, one being the default time zone and another from the available IDs, and then formats a `Calendar` instance with the pattern "h:mma z" using both the `SimpleDateFormat` and `FastDateFormat` to compare the expected and actual values. The issue seems to be related to how the time zone is handled in the `FastDateFormat` class.

Inspecting the `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String)` method, we see that it directly returns an instance from the cache without considering any time zone information. This behavior suggests that the `FastDateFormat` instance generated by this method may not correctly handle the time zone information passed to it, leading to the observed discrepancy in time zone handling in the test case.

To address the issue, it is likely necessary to modify the implementation of the `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String)` method to consider the time zone information when creating the `FastDateFormat` instance.

The recommended method to be fixed is:
```java
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateFormat.getInstance(java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
